areas.name: Invoice generation
areas.note: Legacy emitted a text report to file, printer or screen; modernized emits a QuestPDF document.

areas.name: Reporting and bulk export
areas.note: Legacy print_backlog and print_stock were stubs; both are implemented on the modernized side.

areas.name: Stock catalogue maintenance
areas.note: All four legacy functions were stubs printing 'This option has not been implemented'. The modernized side implements them fully - functionality added by the migration, not ported.

areas.name: Privilege elevation
areas.note: No privilege, role or entitlement concept exists anywhere in the modernized tree. The legacy model was itself broken (the user declared their own privilege level), but it was the only place the system expressed the idea that some users may do more than others.

areas.name: Shell escape / OS command access
areas.note: Ported as a deliberate refusal: the function exists, logs a warning and sets a status message rather than executing anything.

areas.name: Database connection and credentials
areas.note: Remote Informix server over the network became a local SQLite file.

areas.name: Data loading and seeding
areas.note: The same seven .unl files appear byte-identical on both sides.

areas.name: Web transport, hosting and HTTP middleware
areas.note: The entire HTTP surface is new. Every weakness class that requires a browser, a request header, a response header or a network listener lives here and could not have existed in the legacy architecture.

areas.name: Application logging and audit trail
areas.note: The legacy system produced no log output of any kind - only transient terminal messages. Matched application-wide on weakness class rather than by area.
